fix_decisions.claim_text: docs/external/rule-sets.md line 125 said every account identifier is a decimal string so 5 and "5" are written the same way, which is false of the file, where a bare number fails StrictStr validation.
fix_decisions.evidence: Read the loader and confirmed the defect: binding.account_ids is list[RuleSetId] over StrictStr with the decimal pattern, so a bare TOML number does not load and a leading zero is rejected, while a request value is coerced by _decimal_text. Behavior-inert prose cap evaluated and recorded in capped-iter-4.txt: first conjunct and limb one hold, limb two does not, so the cap lands at Important and it stays a reject driver. The sentence now separates the two sides: in the file an identifier is a quoted decimal string, and in a request either the number or the string is read as the same account. Acceptance-criteria comparison: no criterion decides how the page words this, and criterion 2's load-time refusals are unchanged by a documentation edit.

fix_decisions.claim_text: The troubleshooting entry for a startup failure about missing tables or columns offers sqllens validate, which does not run the catalog existence check.
fix_decisions.evidence: Correct, and criterion 6 states the split the page contradicts: the existence check runs in probe_database, which validate invokes only under --check-db. The command now carries --check-db and the surrounding sentence says plain validate only loads the file. The account-not-bound entry's copy of the same command was removed, because it could not reproduce a request refusal either and the entry's own instruction, to check binding.account_ids, needs no command. Cap: first conjunct and limb one hold, limb two does not, so Important stands.

fix_decisions.claim_text: The rule_sets parameter docstring says the flag adds both prompt rules, which is false when the caller supplies a base prompt or no dialect resolves.
fix_decisions.evidence: Correct: build_system_prompt returns a caller-supplied base prompt before any rule is built, and the qualify-every-column rule is appended only inside the resolved-dialect branch. Capped at Suggestion by the behavior-inert prose rule, recorded in capped-iter-4.txt with all three slots held. The docstring now names both conditions, and the same restatement in docs/internal/database-connectors/rule-sets.md line 57 was corrected with it under the class sweep.

fix_decisions.claim_text: The page says serve and validate both print the unconfirmed-set warning; serve logs it.
fix_decisions.evidence: Correct. The sentence now says validate prints a Warning line and serve logs the same warning, so where it appears depends on the logging setup.

fix_decisions.claim_text: Three internal pages state the runner call order without the two new runners.
fix_decisions.evidence: Correct. Each of the four lines is now scoped to a server with no rule-set file and points at the page that gives the rule-set chain, rather than restating that chain in four places.

fix_decisions.claim_text: The architecture tree gains no entry for the two new modules.
fix_decisions.evidence: Correct. The tree now lists src/sqllens/rule_sets.py and names safety/rule_sets.py with the two new runner decorators, matching how it lists the rest of the safety package.

fix_decisions.claim_text: The freshness marker is seven commits behind the branch head.
fix_decisions.evidence: Correct. The marker now names 97783a1, the head the page was last checked against.

fix_decisions.claim_text: _unconfirmed_rule_sets is separated from the preceding definition by one blank line.
fix_decisions.evidence: Correct. It now uses two, like every other top-level definition in the file.

fix_decisions.claim_text: Line 145 tells the operator to restart while the same sentence says the check is retried on the next request.
fix_decisions.evidence: Correct. The sentence now says no restart is needed.

fix_decisions.claim_text: The page said the rule-set key limit counts every _meta key instead of the extras, where both limits apply.
fix_decisions.evidence: Correct, and it was my own iteration-three wording. The line now says a second limit applies beside the extras limit.

fix_decisions.claim_text: The preflight catalog check drops the driver's reason: a non-mismatch failure becomes a PreflightError carrying only the exception's class name, and nothing logs the underlying message.
fix_decisions.evidence: Real and unfixed. Adding a log record here is a behavioural change to the startup path, and this iteration is the loop's last fixing pass before the iteration cap, so making it now would ship an unreviewed behaviour change: the re-review at iteration five covers only what is committed, and the cap leaves no iteration to review a fix made after it. The finding is a diagnosability gap on a path that already fails closed and already names the mismatched table or column for the mismatch case, so leaving it changes no refusal or result. Revisit when the next change touches preflight: log the cause at warning with exc_info before raising, as ensure_catalog_confirmed does.

fix_decisions.claim_text: redacted_refusal_text tests the parse-refusal markers before the check for a reason a guard already logged, so a guard's internal failure quoting a marker would be reported to the model as a statement to rewrite.
fix_decisions.evidence: Real and unfixed, and unreachable today: both reviewers that raised it confirmed no shipped message reaches that order. Reordering the two checks changes which client-facing kind a future message receives, so it is a behavioural change, and the same cap argument as F-8 applies on the loop's last fixing pass. Revisit when the next change touches the redactor: test the already-logged-by-a-guard check first, then the parse markers.

fix_decisions.claim_text: LoadedRuleSets, CatalogConfirmation and RuleSetSelection hold several invariants at call sites rather than in the types.
fix_decisions.evidence: Real and unfixed. Each part is a type-level hardening of state that no shipped path reaches wrongly: the docstring's index wording, the confirmed latch written from preflight without the lock, the unbounded rule-set list, and the unconstrained selection. Moving these invariants into the types changes construction and the preflight write, which is behaviour this loop can no longer re-review before the iteration cap. Revisit together in a follow-up on this module: give rule_sets a minimum length, constrain RuleSetSelection, and make the latch private behind a method that takes its lock.

fix_decisions.claim_text: RefusalRedactingRunner rebuilds the refusal behind its own constructor, and the client-facing kind is chosen by matching text owned by other modules.
fix_decisions.evidence: Real and unfixed, and safe today because the one stateful subclass is re-raised earlier. Both halves are behavioural changes to the refusal path on the loop's last fixing pass, so the same cap argument as F-8 applies. Revisit with F-9, which touches the same function: construct the replacement through the type's own constructor, and give each guard a refusal kind it carries rather than one matched from its message.

fix_decisions.claim_text: RuleSetsConfig can represent a configured-but-unloaded state for an instance not produced by Config's validator, and every downstream gate keys off the loaded value.
fix_decisions.evidence: Real and unfixed. Closing it means validating the pair inside RuleSetsConfig, which changes what construction accepts, and this loop can no longer re-review such a change before the iteration cap. No shipped path builds that instance: every production Config goes through the validator. Revisit with F-10, which is the same class of hardening on the neighbouring module.

src/sqllens/config.py RuleSetsConfig can still represent a configured-but-unloaded state for an instance not produced by Config's validator, and every downstream gate keys off the loaded value.
